item.title: Arsenal goalkeeper Raya absent from training session
item.description: alkeeper David Raya was absent from Arsenal’s open training session on Monday ahead of their Champions League match against Borussia Dortmund after he was forced off during the Gunners’ 2-2 draw at Newcastle. Understudies Kepa Arrizabalaga and Frenchman Illan Meslier took part in the workout as the players were put through their paces ahead of Tuesday’s home match against the Bundesliga side. Raya was replaced by Arrizabalaga in the 70th minute at St James’ Park on Saturday after an apparently innocuous collision with Newcastle striker William Osula. The 31-year-old left the pitch clutching his left arm in visible discomfort with an apparent shoulder problem. Raya played a key role as Arsenal ended a 22-year wait for a Premier League title last season and had started this campaign with seven clean sheets in 10 matches before the match in Newcastle. Raya’s injury came on the day Arsenal welcomed back William Saliba to the matchday squad. The France defender, who was an unused substitute, has not played this season because of an injury. Winger Bukayo Saka, who has been absent since October 21 due to a thigh injury, is still weeks away from a return. Arsenal have a six-point lead at the top of the Premier League table and have enjoyed a strong start to the league phase of the Champions League. item.title: Kenneth Okonkwo tackles Tinubu over Aso Rock water outage
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab A supporter of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Kenneth Okonkwo, has criticised President Bola Tinubu over his reported revelation that water supply was interrupted at the Presidential Villa, questioning how the president could address Nigerians’ needs when basic amenities were not consistently available at his residence. Okonkwo made the remarks in a post on his X account on Monday, where he described Tinubu’s comment about the water interruption at Aso Rock as evidence of what he considered the failure of the president’s administration. He argued that the inability to guarantee steady electricity and water supply at the seat of government raised questions about the administration’s capacity to provide the same necessities for Nigerians. “Without electricity, there is no industrialisation. Without water, there is no life,” he wrote. “If Tinubu could not give himself light and life, are you expecting him to give you what he doesn’t have?” Okonkwo asked. He also linked the development to the 2027 presidential election, warning Nigerians against voting for the All Progressives Congress and Tinubu. “Anyone voting for APC and Tinubu in 2027 is voting for darkness”, he said. Okonkwo subsequently called on Nigerians to support former Vice President Atiku Abubakar in the 2027 election, presenting him as an alternative capable of addressing the country’s electricity and water challenges. “An opportunity to rescue Nigeria has come”, he concluded. item.title: Battle of 20-year-olds at World Chess Championship
item.description: Two 20-year-old chess grandmasters will contest the youngest-ever battle for the ultimate crown when the world championship gets underway on Tuesday. Indian defending champion Gukesh Dommaraju will face challenger Javokhir Sindarov of Uzbekistan in a best-of-14 match in Geneva that could run until December 12. “I don’t think I’m here to defend anything. I’m here to win it all over again. That’s the mindset I’m in,” Gukesh told reporters. He said Sindarov was now “one of the very top players at the very top of his game, so for sure, it’s going to be a real test. “I’m very enthusiastic for this match to test myself against such a strong player, and to see what I’m capable of.” Sindarov is five months older than Gukesh, and both prodigies became grandmasters at 12. Despite Sindarov being on a hot streak and the reigning champion having dipped in form, the challenger rated his chances of victory at 50-50. Sindarov said he had been playing plenty of matches over the past six months, “but still, it’s maybe not enough to prepare for such a hard tournament”. Each daily match can last several hours. With a win scoring one point and a draw a half point, the first player to reach 7.5 points wins the match. If the contest is tied at 7-7, the title is decided on a tie-break. The total prize fund is $2.5 million. The players earn $200,000 for each game they win, with the remainder split equally. – Swiss chocolate chesspieces – Aged just 18, Gukesh beat Chinese title holder Ding Liren in the 2024 world championship in Singapore, becoming the youngest undisputed world champion. Sindarov earned his spot in Geneva by winning the eight-player Candidates Tournament in Cyprus in April. Sindarov is peaking at fourth in the global rankings, while Gukesh has dropped to 26th. Norway’s Magnus Carlsen remains the number one. The championship’s opening ceremony was held on Sunday in the Assembly Hall at the United Nations in Geneva. Two Swiss clocks were brought on the podium containing giant chocolate knights — one white and one dark. Gukesh chose one clock, revealing the dark knight inside, meaning Sindarov will play white in the first game and have the opening move. The match will be played at the Fondation Martin Bodmer overlooking Lake Geneva. item.title: Academy alerts Nigerians as new COVID-19 variant spreads globally
item.description: …Urges vigilance ahead of festive season By Sola Ogundipe The Academy of Medical Sciences of Nigeria has alerted Nigerians to the emergence of a new COVID-19 variant called PJ.2.1, which is spreading across several countries, urging heightened vigilance ahead of the festive season when increased travel and large social gatherings could facilitate transmission. In a public health advisory, the Academy said the World Health Organisation (WHO) had classified PJ.2.1 as a “Variant Under Monitoring”, although its current assessment indicates a low additional global public health risk. According to the advisory signed by the Chairman of the Academy’s Rapid Response Committee, Prof. Boaz Adegboro, and Academy President, Prof. Joseph Ahaneku, the variant was first detected in Ontario, Canada, on May 2, 2026, and has since been reported in the United States, Canada, Spain, France, the Netherlands, Israel, Singapore, Brazil, Argentina, Australia and New Zealand. The WHO had counted sequences from 18 countries as of November 8, 2026. The body, however, cautioned that available evidence remains limited, making continued surveillance necessary to establish the variant’s behaviour and potential impact. It said preliminary studies suggest that PJ.2.1 may spread more efficiently than some other circulating Omicron sub-lineages, but there is currently no evidence that it causes more severe illness. The advisory also said early laboratory findings indicate that existing COVID-19 vaccines remain effective against the variant, with antibodies generated by updated vaccines demonstrating the ability to neutralise it. Describing PJ.2.1 as a descendant of the Omicron JN.1 family, the Academy explained that the variant carries approximately 24 changes in its spike protein compared with its parent lineage. “These mutations have attracted scientific attention because laboratory studies suggest stronger binding to the human ACE2 receptor and more efficient entry into cells, characteristics that could give the variant a transmission advantage,” the statement noted. However, the Academy stressed that increased transmissibility does not necessarily translate into more severe disease. It listed the symptoms as sore throat, fever, cough, runny or blocked nose, fatigue, headache, muscle aches and chills, noting that some patients reportedly experience particularly severe sore throats and prolonged fatigue. The symptoms, it said, are similar to those of common cold and influenza, making laboratory testing necessary to distinguish PJ.2.1 from other respiratory infections. “As at the time of this advisory, there has not been any public report of PJ.2.1 detected in Nigeria. The NCDC continues routine COVID-19 surveillance and has reported sporadic confirmed cases during 2026. Because genomic sequencing in Africa is limited, absence of reports should not be taken as absence of the variant,” the statement noted. item.title: APC’ll win three South-East states; Obi will take Abia, Anambra — Bwala
item.description: The Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Policy Communication, Daniel Bwala, has projected that the All Progressives Congress will win three states in the South-East in the 2027 general elections, while conceding that Peter Obi could retain a stronghold in Abia and Anambra. Bwala made the projection during an interview on Channels Television’s Morning Brief on Monday, where he was asked how the ruling party intended to secure victories in the region. He said Obi’s popularity in the two states could make them difficult for the APC to win, but expressed confidence that the party would prevail in the remaining South-East states. “We will struggle in Abia. You see, in Abia and Anambra, Peter has a very convincing presence. Even in these two states, I am assuming that if we lose, we still come second, which is not a bad thing. Apart from these two states, the remainder of the states, we are winning,” Bwala said. The presidential aide, however, stressed that his assessment was a projection rather than a definitive prediction, noting that different political actors could arrive at varying conclusions from available data. He said the party was willing to acknowledge areas where it might face difficulties rather than make sweeping claims about its chances. “Where we think we may not, and I use the word advisedly because none of what I’m saying is cast in stone, right? It is projection, and two people from the same political party can have different projections based on our own interpretation of data,” he said. Bwala added that admitting potential weaknesses was more honest than claiming the APC would win everywhere, noting that his use of the word “struggle” referred specifically to the party’s chances of winning those states. The presidential adviser also expressed confidence in the APC’s overall prospects ahead of the 2027 elections, dismissing the opposition’s preparedness to challenge the ruling party. “I do not think the opposition is ready. Those who understand the political trajectory can see that they are already facing defeat,” he said. item.title: Boat Mishap: Bayelsa Govt To Commission Marine Taskforce In Search Of Missing Persons
item.description: Governor of Bayelsa State, Douye Diri, is set to commission a marine taskforce to intensify the search for victims of a boat mishap that has claimed over 29 lives in the state. The state’s Commissioner for Marine and Blue Economy, Dr. Faith Godwin, who was a guest on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily on Monday, disclosed that the state government will commission a Safety Marine Taskforce this week as part of the effort to ensure compliance with water transportation safety rules across 30 jetties in Bayelsa State. The development followed Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, with a death toll of 29 recorded so far and over 50 survivors receiving treatment in hospitals. She noted that the collaborative effort to recover more bodies as the search continues. “Actually, the effort is still ongoing. The state government is represented by the Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy by Alsace State in collaboration with the State Emergency Management Agency, as well as Nigerian Police, Nigerian Navy, Security Agency, Civil Defence and the Community Rescue Team, the Ministry Rescue Team also. The efforts are still ongoing to see how we can recover more bodies.” Bayelsa State Commissioner for Marine and Blue Economy, Dr. Faith Zibs Godwin speaking on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily on Monday, November 22, 2026. On why the operator boat which capsized may have flouted safety rules such as overloading, she said, “According to the Maritime Workers Union, as well as the other team who had been at the unit, they said they had to stay clear because the operator at that time felt they didn’t have the right to talk to him. So the boat in question was privately engaged to move persons from that particular location” According to her, the taskforce, which constitutes several government agencies, was set up before the boat incident occurred but will be commissioned this week to ensure safer waterways across the state. “The state government has also constituted, before now, a Marine Safety Task Force, which has to do with coming together of relevant agencies, the National Inland Waterways Representative, that of the Nigerian Navy, the Marine Police Representative and Community Representative to see how they could enforce marine safety measures in our various jetties” She stressed that the task force is empowered to enforce marine safety measures across waterways in the state. ‘The task force has so much to do because it’s an all-inclusive task force in the sense that we have the marine police there, and where operators don’t comply, they would face the law. And our legislative arm too, they are also ready to enact or legislate on certain, you know, state-based policy and laws that we would send to them very soon. So the whole idea is to ensure that what has happened does not repeat itself again.” She added that the Marine taskforce will also be responsible for enforcing boat riverworthiness to ensure safety for passengers. “

item.title: Alice Huang Had Contact With China Spy Agency During Nvidia Boss Affair — Reports
item.description: Alice Huang, the alleged spy at the center of the Nvidia scandal, was in touch with an official from China’s top spy agency during an affair with the chip giant’s former chief executive Jensen Huang, the New York Times reported on Sunday. Alice Huang was this month outed as a suspected Chinese spy, accused of having an affair with Jensen Huang while digging up company secrets for Beijing. She was in contact with an officer of China’s Ministry of State Security from the spring of 2025 until the fall of this year, the Times reported, citing people with knowledge of the intelligence. Alice Huang, who is no relation to Jensen, previously led Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based tech group under investigation for allegedly helping Chinese firms gain access to Nvidia chips, possibly in violation of US export controls. Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang arrives ahead of a state banquet for US President Donald Trump and China’s President Xi Jinping at the Great Hall of the People Beijing on May 14, 2026. (Photo by BRENDAN SMIALOWSKI / AFP) According to the Times, Alice Huang’s contacts with the Chinese spy agency correspond to the affair as well as a period when Megaspeed was acquiring large amounts of advanced Nvidia chips. The Times also reported that US intelligence agencies have gathered evidence that Alice Huang’s business partner Kang Wei — who the newspaper said was often introduced as her husband — worked with the same Chinese spy agency. Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia’s chief executive earlier this month, following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang. He is to be questioned by US lawmakers on December 1 over national security concerns. The upheaval has battered shares of Nvidia which is at the center of an AI boom that has helped propel markets to record highs and boosted economic growth around the globe. item.title: Abia Police condemn officers over pregnant woman’s hospital ordeal
item.description: By Steve Oko The Abia State Police Command has condemned the conduct of some of its personnel who allegedly stopped a man conveying his pregnant wife to hospital over the absence of a displayed vehicle number plate. The incident, captured in a viral video that has generated reactions on social media, involved officers attached to the Surveillance Patrol and Guard Team of Ubakala Divisional Police Station. The man was reportedly taking his pregnant wife to hospital after she began experiencing labour contractions when he encountered the officers, who allegedly insisted on taking him to the police station for driving without a displayed registration number plate. Reacting to the incident, the Police Command said it had identified the officers involved and commenced an investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the encounter and determine their level of responsibility. In a statement issued by the Police Public Relations Officer, Maureen Chinaka, the Command acknowledged that the man was driving without a displayed number plate, contrary to road traffic regulations. It explained that vehicle identification was important, particularly in view of prevailing security challenges, including vehicle theft and the use of unidentified vehicles for criminal activities. The Command, however, said enforcement of traffic regulations should be guided by sound judgment and consideration for human welfare, especially in emergency situations. On the claim that the man’s wife was in labour, the police said preliminary information indicated that she was fine and had not given birth as of the time of the statement. It added that no medical evidence had been presented to substantiate the claim that she was about to deliver. Despite this, the Command expressed displeasure over what it described as the officers’ apparent failure to demonstrate sufficient empathy towards the pregnant woman. The outgoing Commissioner of Police, AIG Wilfred Olutokunbo Afolabi, reiterated that the police had a statutory responsibility not only to prevent and detect crime and maintain law and order but also to protect lives, uphold citizens’ rights and assist people in distress. He stressed that police duties must be discharged with professionalism, empathy, restraint and respect for human dignity. According to him, although the Command would continue to enforce the law, such responsibilities must be carried out with humanity and consideration for prevailing circumstances. The Command assured members of the public that the investigation would be thorough and that appropriate disciplinary measures would be taken if misconduct was established. item.title: Yamal out of Barcelona’s Champions League trip to Sabah
item.description: Lamine Yamal will not travel with his Barcelona team-mates to take on Sabah in the Champions League due to an ankle problem, the Catalan giants said on Monday. item.title: 2027: We’re not jittery; opposition not ready – Bwala
item.description: Sekinat Osundiji Presidential spokesman Daniel Bwala has said the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) is not worried about the opposition ahead of the 2027 general election, insisting that its political rivals are not prepared for the contest. Bwala, Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Policy Communication, stated this during an interview on Channels Television, where he dismissed suggestions that the ruling party was apprehensive about the growing activities of opposition parties. He said the APC was confident about its political standing, adding that the opposition was not ready for the election. “I do not think the opposition is ready. Those who understand the political trajectory can see that they are already facing defeat,” Bwala said. His comments followed questions about President Tinubu’s decision to expand his campaign itinerary beyond the initial 12 states, amid reports of attacks on campaign materials and the president’s convoy. Defending the adjustment, Bwala described it as a strategic decision rather than an indication that the APC was worried about its political opponents. “President Tinubu is not scared. It is a matter of strategy. He is a chess player, who studies the moves of his opponents before deciding on his next move,” he said. He, however, acknowledged that the ruling party was working to secure voters’ support, saying it would be wrong to assume that Nigerians had already decided to re-elect the president. “We are not worried, but we are working hard because we respect the will of the people. We cannot take their votes for granted,” Bwala said. On the political situation in the North, Bwala described the region as a major battleground in the 2027 election, noting that the president’s campaign activities there were part of a deliberate strategy. He rejected suggestions that the North was united against Tinubu, arguing that the position of individual political leaders should not be interpreted as the collective position of the region. “There is no unanimous adoption of a candidate by any bloc in Nigeria, not even in the North. The position of one political leader should not be taken as the position of the entire region,” he said. Bwala also argued that the president had made significant efforts in the South-West, which informed his decision to concentrate more campaign activities in other regions. Addressing Peter Obi’s performance in the 2023 presidential election, the presidential spokesman said the Labour Party candidate benefited from religious sentiments surrounding the APC’s Muslim-Muslim presidential ticket. “Politics is about strategy. In 2023, Peter Obi benefited from the reaction of some Christians to the APC’s Muslim-Muslim ticket. That was one of the factors that shaped the election,” Bwala said. He further claimed that Obi had visited 12 major churches during the previous election cycle but had not maintained the same pattern ahead of 2027. item.title: 2027: Obi’s camp alleges plot to link him with IPOB
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The camp of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has alleged a plot by some political actors to link him with the Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) in a campaign it claims is aimed at weakening his growing support in Northern Nigeria. The Peter Obi Media Office (POMR) raised the alarm on Monday, alleging that individuals within the ruling party and some opposition elements were coordinating a propaganda campaign to portray the former Anambra State governor as sympathetic to Biafran separatism. In a statement signed by its spokesperson, Idris Zekeri, the media office said the alleged campaign was intended to discourage Northern Nigerians, particularly young people, from supporting the Obi-Kwankwaso political movement. It alleged that the campaign could involve sponsored reports in Northern newspapers, interviews on radio stations in the region and coordinated narratives on social media. The media office also cited a claim by a social media personality, Gucci Commando, who allegedly said he had visited IPOB leader, Nnamdi Kanu, in Sokoto and attributed political endorsements in support of Obi to him. However, POMR described the claim as questionable, insisting that allegations of such magnitude required independent verification and should not be presented as established facts. The statement read in part: “The Peter Obi Media Office has expressed grave concern about credible intelligence indicating that certain actors within the ruling party, together with elements of the opposition, have hatched a coordinated anti-Obi propaganda effort aimed at exploiting Nigeria’s delicate ethnic and security divisions. “The alleged purpose of this effort is to falsely link Peter Obi to Biafran separatism and depict him as politically aligned with IPOB leader Nnamdi Kanu, apparently to distance Northern Nigerians, especially young people, from the Obi-Kwankwaso political movement.” The media office maintained that Obi was neither an ethnic nor a religious candidate, describing him as a Nigerian whose political vision and aspirations extended beyond ethnic, religious and regional divisions. It said his political objective was to address the country’s economic, security and governance challenges and build a nation that served the interests of all Nigerians. Zekeri said Obi’s commitment to justice, dialogue, national reconciliation and the rule of law should not be misrepresented as support for separatism. He urged Northern Nigerians not to allow what he described as political propaganda to undermine relationships built around the shared aspiration for a better country. “The Obi-Kwankwaso political engagement is a national initiative, not an ethnic enterprise,” he said. The media office also called on those making allegations linking Obi to separatist activities to provide verifiable evidence rather than rely on insinuations. item.title: 2027: Wabara urges opposition leaders to back consensus candidate
item.description: By Steve Oko, Regional Editor, South-East Former Senate President and Chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) Board of Trustees, Senator Adolphus Wabara, has backed moves by opposition parties to present a consensus presidential candidate for the 2027 general elections, urging political leaders to sacrifice personal ambitions in the interest of rescuing Nigeria. Wabara said opposition unity had become imperative in view of the country’s political and economic challenges, insisting that national survival, democratic stability and the welfare of Nigerians should take precedence over individual presidential ambitions. The former Senate President, who spoke exclusively with Vanguard, urged opposition presidential hopefuls to rise above personal interests, ego and political calculations and rally behind a credible candidate capable of challenging the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). He said the moment demanded political courage, compromise and patriotism, warning that failure by opposition leaders to unite could weaken the country’s democratic space and prolong the hardship facing citizens. His position comes amid ongoing consultations among opposition parties, including the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Allied People’s Movement (APM) and Social Democratic Party (SDP), to forge a common front ahead of the 2027 presidential election. The parties are expected to deepen discussions at a proposed opposition summit scheduled for November 30, where the question of a consensus presidential candidate and a broader framework for political collaboration are expected to feature prominently. Wabara argued that the opposition’s strength lay not in the number of presidential candidates contesting against one another but in its ability to unite behind one candidate with the political capacity, national reach and popular support to challenge the APC. He warned that allowing multiple opposition candidates to divide the votes of Nigerians seeking change could give the ruling party an electoral advantage without a meaningful challenge. According to him, the overriding objective should be to rescue Nigeria from the control of a few political interests while millions of citizens grapple with economic hardship, insecurity, unemployment and declining living standards. Describing the country’s situation as a threat to democracy, Wabara called on opposition leaders to demonstrate statesmanship by supporting whoever emerges as the consensus candidate, even if doing so requires them to shelve their presidential ambitions. He said: “Nigeria is currently under captivity by a few cabal who should have no business being in power. Our democracy is at stake, and now is the time for uncommon sacrifices for our national survival. “I want the progressive opposition presidential flag bearers to put Nigeria above their individual interests. Let them present the best among them while others step down and rally support for the consensus

item.title: Troops clear suspected IPOB/ESN camp, neutralise IEDs in Imo
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of the Nigerian Army, working alongside other security agencies, have cleared additional sections of a suspected Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) and Eastern Security Network (ESN) camp in Imo State, uncovering and neutralising improvised explosive devices (IEDs). The operation, conducted on November 21 around Awomama in Oru East Local Government Area, was part of ongoing security offensives launched on November 16 and 17, according to the Army. The joint operation involved troops of the 34 Artillery Brigade and personnel of the Nigerian Navy, Nigerian Air Force, Nigeria Police Force, Department of State Services (DSS) and Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC). Security sources said the joint team advanced into the Tango 2 and Tango 3 sections of the suspected camp at about 6:30 a.m., where they discovered that the locations had been heavily fortified with explosives. With the support of Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) personnel, the troops located and successfully neutralised the improvised explosive devices. The operation also led to the recovery of two battery components suspected to have been used to trigger the explosives. The clearance operation is part of sustained efforts by security agencies to dismantle suspected criminal hideouts and prevent attacks in the area. item.title: PANDEF mourns Bayelsa boat accident victims, urges coastal roads
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF) has mourned victims of the boat accident around Oweikorogha Community in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, which reportedly claimed several lives, including youths and children. The socio-political organisation also renewed its call on the Federal Government and governments of oil-producing states to prioritise the construction of roads and bridges to connect isolated coastal communities and reduce their dependence on water transportation. PANDEF, in a statement signed by its National Chairman, Ambassador Godknows Igali, said it received the news of the accident, which occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, with shock and sadness. The organisation described the incident as heartbreaking and commiserated with the affected families, the Bayelsa State Government, residents of Southern Ijaw and the affected communities. It said the tragedy reinforced its longstanding position that inadequate road infrastructure had left many coastal communities with limited transportation options, making water travel a necessity for their residents. According to PANDEF, the Federal Government should, as an interim measure, support state governments in acquiring adequate seaworthy vessels to meet the transportation needs of coastal communities. The organisation also called on emergency relief agencies, security agencies and regulatory authorities to work with the Bayelsa State Government to provide assistance to survivors and bereaved families. It urged the relevant authorities to strengthen enforcement of water transportation safety regulations, including compliance with passenger safety protocols, the use of appropriate safety equipment and the operation of vessels that meet prescribed seaworthiness standards. PANDEF said measures must be taken to prevent a recurrence of such tragedies, stressing the need for improved transportation infrastructure and stricter safety standards across the coastal areas. The statement read in part: “While mourning this tragic loss, PANDEF calls on the relevant emergency relief agencies, security agencies and regulatory authorities to work closely with the Bayelsa State Government to ensure that all necessary measures are taken to assuage the impact on survivors and bereaved families. “More importantly, [they should] take all necessary measures to prevent a recurrence of such tragedies.” The organisation expressed solidarity with the victims’ families and the people of Bayelsa State, praying for the repose of the souls of the deceased and comfort for those affected by the tragedy. item.title: Fire Destroys Over 100 Shops At Kano Fish Market, Traders Count Losses
item.description: A fire outbreak at Kano Fish Market along Zaria Road has destroyed more than 100 shops, leaving traders counting losses estimated to run into billions of naira. The fire reportedly broke out at about 9:00 p.m. on Sunday, near Kano Line Motor Park, spreading across sections of the market and destroying shops, containers and goods. Reports indicate that approximately 150 shops and 200 containers were affected by the inferno, with some traders reportedly losing goods valued at millions of naira. Traders trying to salvage what is left after the fire One of the affected traders, Usman Sani, recounted how the fire spread through the market, destroying shops and goods before traders could salvage their belongings. “We received the news of the fire and rushed to the market, but by the time we got here, the flames had already spread. Many shops were affected, and traders lost goods worth millions of naira. The situation is heartbreaking,” he said. The huge fire on Sunday, November 22, 2026, as it razes the fish shop in Kano State. Another trader, Musa Inuwa, described the incident as a major setback for those who depend on the market for their livelihood. “Many of us depend entirely on this business to feed our families. We have lost our goods and capital, and we do not know where to start from. We are appealing to the government to come to our assistance,” he said. The affected traders are appealing to the Kano State Government and relevant authorities for urgent intervention to support those who lost their businesses. The Kano State Fire Service reportedly received a distress call at about 9:58 p.m. and deployed personnel to the scene, arriving four minutes later. item.title: UK Digging New Reservoirs To Fight Persistent Droughts
item.description: Britain has long had a reputation for rain. But as it adapts to a warmer, drier climate, the UK is racing to complete a huge new reservoir, its first in over three decades. Bulldozers have been digging up the ground for the vast £800-million ($1 billion) Havant Thicket project near the southern coastal port of Portsmouth. Like much of Europe, Britain endured record-breaking heat this summer and, despite the return of rains as the country moves into winter, parts are still grappling with drought conditions. “We’ve got increasing problems with our water security in the UK,” climate scientist Hannah Cloke from Reading University told AFP. “We need to really think about how we’re storing that water because this problem is only going to get worse.” Scientists have warned extreme weather events are likely to become more frequent and more intense as the global climate changes. Workers carry out construction work at the site of the new Havant Thicket Reservoir in Hampshire, southern England, on November 5, 2026. Photo by CARLOS JASSO / AFP By mid-November, almost all of England remained in drought, with some areas classified as suffering severe drought, according to the Environment Agency. Potentially exacerbating matters, existing reservoirs were only 60 percent full, 19 percentage points below the seasonal average. For policymakers, the situation poses a longer-term challenge as the thirst for water increases with a rising population and the growth of heavy water-using industries such as data centres. Under England’s National Framework for Water Resources published in 2025, the country could face a daily water supply shortfall of five billion litres (1.3 billion gallons) by 2055, with resources under pressure. At the sprawling Havant Thicket site, Portsmouth Water chief executive Bob Taylor said the industry was waking up to the scale of the challenge after successive droughts and hot summers. Workers carry out construction work at the site of the new Havant Thicket Reservoir in Hampshire, southern England, on November 5, 2026. Photo by CARLOS JASSO / AFP The issue, he stressed, was not necessarily how much rain falls over the course of a year, but when it falls. Winters are becoming wetter, while summers are increasingly dry. “Without reservoirs you can’t store that intense rainfall and put it somewhere where it can be used at another time,” Taylor said. The new reservoir will eventually hold up to 8.7 billion litres of water, helping secure supplies for hundreds of thousands of people. Fed in part by winter surpluses from a major spring already tapped by Portsmouth Water, it has become one of the flagship projects in a broader shift in Britain’s water strategy. The government has approved the construction of nine major reservoirs by 2050, and last year relaxed planning rules to speed up projects after decades of under-investment in water infrastructure. Together, the future reservoirs could deliver an additional 670 million litres of water per day. ‘

item.title: Alleged Sexual Assault: Daura Emirate Probes Viral Video As Tourist Accuses Emir of Inappropriate Conduct
item.description: Tension has gripped Daura in Katsina State following the emergence of a viral video in which a foreign female tourist accused the Emir of Daura, Alhaji Dr. Faruk Umar Faruk, of inappropriate sexual conduct during a visit to his palace. The allegations, which have generated widespread reactions on social media, are currently under review by the Daura Emirate Council, which says it is investigating the authenticity of the video and the claims made by the tourist. The woman, identified as Mirka and known on Instagram by the handle @beduinqa, posted the video after completing a 30-day tour of different parts of Nigeria. In a statement accompanying the footage, she alleged that the incident occurred on Saturday, November 14, 2026, when she visited the Emir’s palace in Daura. According to her account, she was ushered into a large room where she met privately with the Emir. She alleged that during their conversation, the Emir held her hand and began playing with it despite her objections. Mirka claimed she repeatedly asked him to stop, writing: “I told him, ‘Your Highness, no, no, no. You should not be touching me like that.’ But he just laughed.” She further alleged that as the meeting ended, the Emir hugged her, kissed her on the cheeks and touched her breast without her consent. The tourist said the encounter left her shocked, disgusted and emotionally distressed, adding that it was the only alleged incident of sexual harassment she experienced throughout her month-long tour of Nigeria. She also claimed she was able to capture the encounter using a pair of Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses equipped with a built-in camera, and alleged that she may not have been the first woman to experience such conduct but might have been the first to record it. Reacting to the development, the spokesman of the Daura Emirate Council, Ibrahim Usman Murtala, confirmed in a telephone interview with our correspondent on Monday that the Emirate was aware of the viral video. Emir of Daura, Alhaji Dr. Faruk Umar Faruk He said the Emirate had commenced a review of the footage to determine its authenticity and ascertain whether it had been altered or manipulated using any form of technology. According to him, the Emirate will issue an official statement after concluding its internal review of the matter. As of the time of filing this report, neither the Emir of Daura nor the Daura Emirate Council had issued a substantive response to the specific allegations made by the tourist. The tourist, who identified herself on Instagram as @beduinqa, alleged in a viral video that the 92-year-old monarch fondled her hand and other body parts.
